# `tfctl api`

The `tfctl api` command performs any HCP Terraform API v2 request, or searches and inspects API operations.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl api PATH [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl api` command performs any HCP Terraform API v2 request. This is a low-level command that provides direct access to the HCP Terraform API, allowing you to make any API call that the HCP Terraform API supports.

For common operations, consider using the higher-level [`tfctl get`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/get) and [`tfctl create`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/create) commands, which provide a more user-friendly interface.

The `tfctl api schema` command group includes subcommands to allow you to search and inspect API operations using HCP Terraform's OpenAPI specification. 

## Arguments

- `PATH`: (Required) API path or URL. Supports `{name}` path parameter name resolution.

## Command groups

- [`schema`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/api/schema) - Search and inspect API operations

## Available options

The `tfctl api` command supports the following options.

| Option | Description | Default | Required |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------|
| `--all` | Fetch all records. May be slow for large amounts of data. Limited to 2000 records. | None | No |
| `-a, --attribute=KEY=VALUE` | Attribute for JSON:API request bodies. Implies POST method. Can be repeated to set multiple attributes. | None | No |
| `-f, --field=KEY=VALUE` | Add a query parameter to the request URL. Can be repeated to add multiple query parameters. | None | No |
| `-H, --header='name: value'` | Request header. Can be repeated to add multiple headers. | None | No |
| `-i, --input=BODY` | Raw JSON request body (or `-` to read from stdin). | None | No |
| `-X, --method=METHOD` | HTTP method to use (e.g., GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE). | Inferred from flags | No |
| `-n, --page-number` | Page number to return. Ignored if `--all` is set. | 1 | No |
| `-s, --page-size` | Limit the number of records to return. Default varies by resource. Ignored if `--all` is set. | Varies by resource | No |
| `-p, --pathparam=KEY=VALUE` | Provide a hint for path parameter resolution. The HCP Terraform API typically requires a resource ID for resource-specific requests. Allows automatic resolution to resource ID from name (workspaces, teams, projects, varsets). Can be repeated to set multiple path parameters. | Auto-resolved from profile/configuration | No |
| `-t, --type=TYPE` | Resource type for `--attribute` JSON:API request bodies. This value is inferred from the path whenever possible. | Inferred from path | No |

### Pagination

Commands that list multiple resources are paginated. For details on pagination options and behavior, refer to [Pagination](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#pagination).

### Global flags

Refer to [Global flags reference](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#global-flags) for information about flags you can use with all commands.

## Path parameter resolution

Use `{name}` placeholders for path parameters and `-p` to set their values:

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/runs -p workspace=my-workspace
```

If you do not provide a value for a named path parameter, the tfctl CLI attempts to automatically determine their values from the active profile or local Terraform configuration, when present.

- `{organization}`: Resolves from active profile or local Terraform config
- `{workspace}`: Resolves workspace name to ID (ws- prefix)
- `{team}`: Resolves team name to ID (team- prefix)
- `{project}`: Resolves project name to ID (prj- prefix)
- `{varset}`: Resolves variable set name to ID (varset- prefix)

The tfctl CLI automatically resolves workspace, team, project, and varset names to their IDs, if required.

## Examples

The following examples demonstrate how to make direct API calls to HCP Terraform.

### Discovering API operations

Before making API calls, use the [`tfctl api schema`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/api/schema) commands to discover available operations.

#### Search for operations

Search for workspace-related operations.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api schema search workspace
```

#### Get operation details

View the schema for a specific operation by operation ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api schema get getWorkspace
```

### Read resources

List and display information about individual resources by specifying the path along with any required parameters.

#### List workspaces in the active profile's organization

List all workspaces in the organization configured for your active profile:

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/workspaces
```

#### List runs for a workspace by name

List runs for a workspace by name. Replace `<WORKSPACE_NAME>` with your workspace's name.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/runs -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_NAME>
```

#### List runs for a workspace by ID

List runs for a workspace using its workspace ID. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/runs -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID>
```

#### Get workspace details

Get detailed information about a specific workspace. Replace `<WORKSPACE_NAME_OR_ID>` with your workspace's name or ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_NAME_OR_ID>
```

#### Get run details

Get detailed information about a specific run. Replace `<RUN_ID>` with your run's ID:

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /runs/<RUN_ID>
```

#### List all records with pagination

Fetch all workspaces (up to 2000 records). For details on pagination options, refer to [Pagination](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#pagination).

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/workspaces --all
```

#### Filter results with query parameters

List workspaces filtered by name. Replace `<SEARCH_TERM>` with your search term.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/workspaces -f 'search[name]=<SEARCH_TERM>'
```

### Creating resources

To create resources, most API calls accept POST attributes with the `-a` flag, or JSON:API request bodies with the `-i` flag.

#### Create a project

Create a project using the `-a` flag to set attributes. Replace `<PROJECT_NAME>` with a valid name for your project.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/projects -a name=<PROJECT_NAME>
```

#### Create a workspace

Create a workspace with multiple attributes. Replace `<WORKSPACE_NAME>` with a valid workspace name that does not already exist for the given organization.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/workspaces \
  -a name=<WORKSPACE_NAME> \
  -a description="Production workspace" \
  -a auto-apply=true
```

#### Create a workspace variable using attributes

Create a workspace variable using the `-a` flag. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/vars \
  -a key=AWS_REGION \
  -a value=us-west-2 \
  -a category=terraform \
  -a description="AWS region for resources" \
  -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID>
```

#### Create a workspace variable using a JSON:API request body

Create a workspace variable using a full JSON:API request body. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/vars -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID> -i '{ "data": {
  "type":"vars",
  "attributes": {
    "key":"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID",
    "value":"FOOBARBAZQUX",
    "category":"env",
    "sensitive":true
  }
}}'
```

### Updating resources

Use the `-X PATCH` flag to send PATCH requests to update resources.

#### Update workspace settings

Update workspace settings using attributes. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID> \
  -X PATCH \
  -a auto-apply=true \
  -a terraform-version=1.5.0
```

#### Update a variable

Update a variable's value. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID and `<VARIABLE_ID>` with your variable's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/vars/{variable} \
  -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID> \
  -p variable=<VARIABLE_ID> \
  -X PATCH \
  -a value=new-value
```

### Deleting resources

Use the `-X DELETE` flag to send DELETE requests to delete resources. The CLI will prompt the user to confirm before deleting resources.

#### Delete a workspace

Delete a workspace. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} -p <WORKSPACE_ID> -X DELETE
```

#### Delete a variable

Delete a variable. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID and `<VARIABLE_ID>` with your variable's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/vars/{variable} \
  -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID> \
  -p variable=<VARIABLE_ID> \
  -X DELETE
```

### Run operations

The tfctl CLI provides the [`tfctl run`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/run) command group to start and view the status of workspace runs. You can also access the runs API directly by path.

#### Start a run

Start a run in a workspace. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /runs -X POST -i '{
  "data": {
    "type": "runs",
    "attributes": {
      "message": "Triggered via tfctl api"
    },
    "relationships": {
      "workspace": {
        "data": {
          "type": "workspaces",
          "id": "ws-gXocZwBXsYeEZkW4"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}'
```

#### Apply a run

Apply a run that is waiting for confirmation. Replace `<RUN_ID>` with your run's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /runs/{run}/actions/apply -p run=<RUN_ID> -X POST -i '{"data":{"type":"runs"}}'
```

#### Cancel a run

Cancel a running or pending run. Replace `<RUN_ID>` with your run's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /runs/{run}/actions/cancel -p run=<RUN_ID> -X POST -i '{"data":{"type":"runs"}}'
```

### Extract specific fields with jq

Get just the workspace name using the `--jq` flag. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID> --jq '.data.attributes.name'
```

### List all workspace names

List all workspace names in your organization.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/workspaces --jq '.data[].attributes.name'
```

### Capture run ID for later use

Start a run and capture its ID.

```shell-session
$ RUN_ID=$(tfctl api /runs -i '{...}' --jq '.data.id')
$ echo "Started run: $RUN_ID"
```

### Chain operations

Create a workspace and then create a variable in it.

```shell-session
# Create workspace and capture ID
$ WORKSPACE_ID=$(tfctl api /organizations/{organization}/workspaces \
  -a name=my-workspace \
  --jq '.data.id')

# Create variable in the new workspace
$ tfctl api /vars \
  -a key=ENVIRONMENT \
  -a value=production \
  -a category=terraform \
  -p workspace=$WORKSPACE_ID
```

### Use custom headers

Make a request with custom headers. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} \
  -H 'X-Custom-Header: value' \
  -p workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID>
```
